## Documents & policy guidance
{: #documents-policy-guidance }

[✎ Edit](https://github.com/litlfred/folio-assistant-core/edit/main/processes/content/authoring-a-document.bpmn){: .fa-node-edit title="Edit processes/content/authoring-a-document.bpmn" data-fa-link="edit" data-src="processes/content/authoring-a-document.bpmn" data-repo="litlfred/folio-assistant-core" } <span class="fa-qa-badges"><button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-kg" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="kg" data-qa-key="documents-policy-guidance.kg" data-qa-label="Knowledge-graph QA" data-qa-noun="diagram" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/folio-assistant-core/concepts-document-content-type/documents-policy-guidance.kg.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/folio-assistant-core/concepts-document-content-type/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Knowledge-graph QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Knowledge-graph QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">KG</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button></span>

**Skill package:** `folio-document-adapter` ·
**Adapter:** `document` ·
**Guide:** [Writing a document](../guides/writing-a-document.html)

Structured prose: health-policy guidance (an L1 guideline, say), a standard, a
report, a handbook, a book chapter. Everything a paper is, minus the formal
layer — and therefore minus the two toolchains that serve it.

- **Source model** — the same tree of typed *blocks* as a paper, restricted to
  the kinds whose content is prose rather than a formal claim: `prose`,
  `example`, `remark`, `algorithm`, `simulator`, `equation`, `diagram`,
  `table`, `figure`, `recommendation`.
- **Rendering** — `document_render_md` assembles the folio into one Markdown
  file; `document_render_html` and `document_render_pdf` take it through
  pandoc. The PDF path uses an HTML engine (weasyprint, prince, wkhtmltopdf)
  and **never** falls back to `latexmk`.
- **Enforcement** — `content_profile_check` rejects a math kind, a `lean`
  field or a `.lean` sibling, and runs on every `content_validate`.

Relevant skill schemas:
[`document-authoring`]({{ '/reference/skills/document-authoring.html' | relative_url }}),
[`document-structure`]({{ '/reference/skills/document-structure.html' | relative_url }}),
[`normative-statements`]({{ '/reference/skills/normative-statements.html' | relative_url }}),
[`document-publishing`]({{ '/reference/skills/document-publishing.html' | relative_url }}).

### Carrying a normative statement
{: #carrying-a-normative-statement data-fa-label="sec:content-types-carrying-a-normative-statement" }

[✎ Edit](https://github.com/litlfred/folio-assistant-core/edit/main/docs/source/concepts-document-content-type/carrying-a-normative-statement.md){: .fa-node-edit title="Edit docs/source/concepts-document-content-type/carrying-a-normative-statement.md" data-fa-link="edit" data-src="docs/source/concepts-document-content-type/carrying-a-normative-statement.md" data-repo="litlfred/folio-assistant-core" } <span class="fa-qa-badges"><button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-block" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="block" data-qa-key="carrying-a-normative-statement.block" data-qa-label="Content QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/folio-assistant-core/concepts-document-content-type/carrying-a-normative-statement.block.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/folio-assistant-core/concepts-document-content-type/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Content QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Content QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">QA</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button> <button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-translation" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="translation" data-qa-key="carrying-a-normative-statement.translation" data-qa-label="Translation QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/folio-assistant-core/concepts-document-content-type/carrying-a-normative-statement.translation.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/folio-assistant-core/concepts-document-content-type/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Translation QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Translation QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">TR</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button></span>

A recommendation, requirement or rule is the block readers cite and
implementers trace to. It wants a label, a stable identity and a place in the
dependency graph — everything a `theorem` has — but nothing proves it; its
authority is the issuing body's.

Its carrier is the **`recommendation` block kind**: one statement per block,
with a label, a title, and its strength as a code in a declared code list. The
[`normative-statements`]({{ '/reference/skill-instructions/normative-statements.html' | relative_url }})
skill states the convention. Do not use `definition`: it is a math kind whose
`lean` field is required.
